speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a significant medical history and are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; can you tell me if these symptoms have been progressive over time or if they appeared suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. You mentioned the symptoms are on the right side; are they accompanied by any weakness, numbness, or vision changes? Additionally, have you noticed any issues with your speech or swallowing recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain axial/coronal/sagittal.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and use of natalizumab, are you experiencing any new urinary retention, visual disturbances, or optic neuritis symptoms?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.

The imaging results provided confirm multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, which is the classic radiographic presentation of PML. Given your history of natalizumab use, this is a known, serious adverse effect requiring immediate cessation of the drug and management by neurology. Do you have any other neurological symptoms or a family history of similar conditions?
